70655-the-hermit-s-cave.title: Theodore and Jack.
70655-the-hermit-s-cave.creator: Eleanora H. Stooke,
70655-the-hermit-s-cave.description: A book by Eleanora H. Stooke,. "Well, Master Theodore," was the reply, in rather injured tones, "I suppose it is as God pleases, anyway. I may dig, and plant, and prune, and tend the garden with all my strength, but it's all no good if God doesn't help. That's my experience, sir, and I've lived nigh upon seventy years, and more than fifty of those years I've been working in these here gardens. You don't find many of my sort now-a-days," he added with conscious pride.

arxiv-2112-10631.title: Infinite energy cavitating solutions: a variational approach
arxiv-2112-10631.creator: Pablo V. Negrón–Marrero, Jeyabal Sivaloganathan
arxiv-2112-10631.description: Abstract We study the phenomenon of cavitation for the displacement boundary-value problem of radial, isotropic compressible elasticity for a class of stored energy functions of the form W ⁡ ( F ) + h ⁡ ( det F ) W(F)+h(\det F) , where W W grows like ‖ F ‖ n \left\|F\right\|^{n} , and n n is the space dimension.

arxiv-2304-08952.title: A Hyper-network Based End-to-end Visual Servoing with Arbitrary Desired Poses
arxiv-2304-08952.creator: Hongxiang Yu, Anzhe Chen, Kechun Xu, Zhongxiang Zhou, Wei Jing, Yue Wang, Rong Xiong
arxiv-2304-08952.description: Abstract Recently, several works achieve end-to-end visual servoing (VS) for robotic manipulation by replacing traditional controller with differentiable neural networks, but lose the ability to servo arbitrary desired poses. This letter proposes a differentiable architecture for arbitrary pose servoing: a hyper-network based neural controller (HPN-NC).

arxiv-2307-15045.title: A Transformer-based Approach for Arabic Offline Handwritten Text Recognition
arxiv-2307-15045.creator: \au Saleh Momeni 1 \au Bagher BabaAli 2
arxiv-2307-15045.description: Abstract Handwriting recognition is a challenging and critical problem in the fields of pattern recognition and machine learning, with applications spanning a wide range of domains. In this paper, we focus on the specific issue of recognizing offline Arabic handwritten text.

arxiv-2308-00088.title: The physics of optical computing
arxiv-2308-00088.creator: Peter L. McMahon
arxiv-2308-00088.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Peter L. McMahon. There has been a resurgence of interest in optical computing over the past decade, both in academia and in industry, with much of the excitement centered around special-purpose optical computers for neural-network processing. Optical computing has been a topic of periodic study for over 50 years, including for neural networks three decades ago, and a wide variety of optical-computing schemes and architectures have been proposed.

arxiv-2309-03291.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Arwa Dabbech, Amir Aghabiglou, Chung San Chu, Yves Wiaux. A novel deep learning paradigm for synthesis imaging by radio interferometry in astronomy was recently proposed, dubbed “ R esidual-to- R esidual D NN series for high- D ynamic range imaging” ( R2D2 ). In this work, we start by shedding light on R2D2’s algorithmic structure, interpreting it as a learned version of CLEAN with minor cycles substituted with a deep neural network (DNN) whose training is iteration-specific.

arxiv-2407-18504.title: Multilevel Monte Carlo in Sample Average Approximation: Convergence, Complexity and Application
arxiv-2407-18504.creator: Devang Sinha, Siddhartha P. Chakrabarty
arxiv-2407-18504.description: Abstract In this paper, we examine the Sample Average Approximation (SAA) procedure within a framework where the Monte Carlo estimator of the expectation is biased. We also introduce Multilevel Monte Carlo (MLMC) in the SAA setup to enhance the computational efficiency of solving optimization problems.

arxiv-2503-04500.title: ReynoldsFlow: Physics-Inspired Spatiotemporal Flow Representation for Video Understanding
arxiv-2503-04500.creator: Yu-Hsi Chen, Ching-Kai Lin, PingKong Huang, Chin-Tien Wu 🖂
arxiv-2503-04500.description: Abstract Video understanding has largely relied on deep spatiotemporal architectures, including 3D convolutional networks and optical flow (OF) based models. While effective, these methods are often computationally expensive and depend on heuristic motion representations that are sensitive to illumination, scale, and structural changes.

arxiv-2503-09011.title: Word2winners at SemEval-2025 Task 7: Multilingual and Crosslingual Fact-Checked Claim Retrieval
arxiv-2503-09011.creator: Amirmohammad Azadi, Sina Zamani, Mohammadmostafa Rostamkhani, Sauleh Eetemadi
arxiv-2503-09011.description: Abstract This paper describes our system for SemEval 2025 Task 7: Previously Fact-Checked Claim Retrieval. The task requires retrieving relevant fact-checks for a given input claim from the extensive, multilingual MultiClaim dataset, which comprises social media posts and fact-checks in several languages.

arxiv-2505-06386.title: \system : Low-Friction, Interactive Embedding Visualization
arxiv-2505-06386.creator: Donghao Ren Apple, Fred Hohman ∗ Apple, Halden Lin Apple, Dominik Moritz Apple
arxiv-2505-06386.description: Abstract Embedding projections are popular for visualizing large datasets and models. However, people often encounter “friction” when using embedding visualization tools: (1) barriers to adoption, e.g., tedious data wrangling and loading, scalability limits, no integration of results into existing workflows, and (2) limitations in possible analyses, without integration with external tools to additionally show coordinated views of metadata.

arxiv-2602-18969.creator: Paweł Borówka, Angela Ortega
arxiv-2602-18969.description: Abstract . We characterize the moduli space of étale Klein coverings (i.e. Galois with deck group ℤ 2 2 \mathbb{Z}_{2}^{2} ) of hyperelliptic curves of genus 3. We prove that the Prym map on each component is injective. As an application, we show that the Prym map of étale Klein coverings of genus 3 curves is generically finite.
